organizations.What they build: Maker of the cheapest widely sold legged robots: Go2 robot dog (from $1,600), R1 humanoid (from $4,900), G1 humanoid (from $13.5K), H1/H2 full-size humanoids, B2/A2 industrial quadrupeds, dexterous hands and LiDARs. Listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in Aug 2026 (IPO priced at ~61bn yuan / ~$9bn valuation).
organizations._relationship_reason: Realistic only as a hardware supplier (buy a Go2/R1/G1 through a European reseller, maybe an education discount); a sponsorship from Hangzhou for a 15-student Paris lab is unlikely.

organizations.What they build: Humanoid and service-robot company: Walker S2 industrial humanoid with autonomous hot-swappable battery, in mass production since Nov 2025 with orders reported above 800m yuan; also education and consumer robots. Signed a cooperation deal with Airbus in Jan 2026.
organizations._relationship_reason: Has a European commercial footprint (Airbus deal) so a talk or visit at a trade fair is plausible; hardware is far above our budget.

organizations.What they build: Founded 2023; world's largest humanoid shipper in H1 2026 per industry data cited by Global Times. Builds humanoids (A-series, X-series) and open-sources robot-learning assets: the AgiBot World dataset and the GO-1 foundation model. Began Hong Kong IPO process in Jul 2026; Oct 2026 round reported at ~RMB 50bn valuation.
organizations._relationship_reason: Its open dataset and GO-1 model can be used directly in our LeRobot-style projects; contributing benchmarks or fine-tunes is the realistic 'partnership'. Direct sponsorship unlikely.

organizations.What they build: Wheeled humanoid robots (G1, S1, ET1) driven by its own embodied foundation models (AstraBrain series). Raised ~$362M in early 2026 (investors incl. National AI Industry Investment Fund, Sinopec), described as China's highest-valued unlisted humanoid firm.
organizations._relationship_reason: Strong research culture (VLA models) makes papers/talks the only realistic touchpoint; no European presence found.

organizations.What they build: Started in rehabilitation robotics and now builds GR-series humanoids; ranked 6th globally in 2025 humanoid shipments (Omdia). In 2026 built Meta's 'Max' humanoid in ~3 months. Investors include SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and Prosperity7.
organizations._relationship_reason: Possible research-hardware vendor; the Meta collaboration shows it works with foreign AI teams, but a student lab would only be a customer.

organizations.What they build: EV maker XPeng's robotics unit; its IRON general-purpose humanoid rolled off a dedicated production line in Sep 2026 (core process automation >80%).
organizations._relationship_reason: XPeng sells cars in Europe, so engineers may speak at European events; otherwise out of reach.

organizations.What they build: Collaborative robot arms (CR/CRA/Nova series), education desktop arms (Magician, Magician E6, MG400), the X-Trainer teleoperation platform for AI data collection, and ATOM full-size industrial humanoid (third batch in mass delivery from Feb 2026).
organizations._relationship_reason: Has a large education business and European distribution (multi-language site); an education discount or loan of desktop arms is a realistic ask.

organizations.What they build: Mobile robot bases (SCOUT, RANGER, BUNKER, HUNTER, LIMO) and low-cost arms for physical-AI research: PiPER 6-DoF arm (4.2 kg, 1.5 kg payload, ±0.1 mm, ~$2,499), NERO, Cobot Magic / Mobile ALOHA kits, Pika data-collection kit. Open SDKs on GitHub.
organizations._relationship_reason: Closest Chinese match to our wedge: PiPER and Cobot Magic are research arms used for imitation learning; open SDK; a discount or co-marketing for open-source LeRobot integration is plausible.

organizations.What they build: Quadruped robots (Jueying Lite3, X30, LYNX M20 wheel-legged), DR02 all-weather humanoid and J-series joint modules; filed for a 2.5bn-yuan STAR Market IPO in May 2026.
organizations._relationship_reason: Lite3 is a research quadruped alternative to Unitree; buying one is the only realistic link.

organizations.What they build: Wheeled dual-arm R1 robots (from $39,999), LEMO A1Z 6-DoF arm (from $2,999) and LEMO desktop dual-arm platform, plus open-source VLA models (G0, G0.5) in the GalaxeaVLA repo. Raised a 1bn-yuan Series B in Feb 2026 (10bn-yuan valuation).
organizations._relationship_reason: Sells developer-oriented arms internationally and open-sources its VLA; benchmarking G0 on our low-cost arms is a natural collaboration hook.

organizations.What they build: Tsinghua University spinout building STAR1 and L7 humanoids and dexterous hands; raised ~500m yuan Series A in Jul 2025.
organizations._relationship_reason: Tsinghua-linked research team; academic talks are the only realistic contact.

organizations.What they build: KUAVO humanoid series (KUAVO 4Pro, KUAVO 5) sold as research/education and service platforms; 4th in 2025 humanoid shipments (Omdia, ~500 units); filed for a ChiNext IPO in May 2026.
organizations._relationship_reason: Research-platform vendor only.

organizations.Organization: Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics (X-Humanoid)
organizations.What they build: State-backed humanoid innovation center: Tiangong humanoids (TianGong 3.0 in mass delivery H2 2026), embodied-AI software, and the open RoboMIND dataset (300k+ dual-arm trajectories, 700+ tasks; 20m downloads by Sep 2026).
organizations._relationship_reason: Open dataset and open-source community are usable now; formal partnership with a foreign student lab unlikely.

organizations.What they build: Non-profit AI institute; releases open embodied-AI 'brain' models such as RoboBrain 2.0 (7B checkpoint on Hugging Face, Jun 2025) and later RoboBrain 2.5, trained with its FlagScale framework.
organizations._relationship_reason: Open models we can use and cite; researchers publish at international conferences, so a remote talk is possible.

organizations.What they build: Major state AI lab whose InternRobotics group open-sources InternVLA-M1 (spatially guided VLA, MIT license) and the InternUtopia (ex-GRUtopia) embodied-AI simulation platform.
organizations._relationship_reason: Fully open code; contributing or reproducing their VLA on our hardware is the realistic engagement.

organizations.What they build: Warehouse robotics: shelf/tote/pallet AMRs, sorting robots, picking robot arm and fleet software; listed in Hong Kong in Jul 2025.
organizations._relationship_reason: Has European customers/offices for logistics; a case-study talk is plausible, not hardware.

organizations.What they build: Leading domestic industrial-robot and servo maker (called 'first share of industrial robots'); in Sep 2026 consolidated a humanoid robot business by acquiring Estun Kuozhuo.
organizations._relationship_reason: No realistic relationship for a student lab; listed for value-chain context (industrial arms and motion control).

organizations.What they build: Annual Beijing robotics expo and conference; 2026 edition (19-23 Aug) showed 3,000+ products. Shares the season with the World Humanoid Robot Games (2nd edition Aug 2026).
organizations._relationship_reason: Useful to track product launches; travel to Beijing is out of budget for us.

organizations.What they build: Shanghai's annual AI conference; 2026 edition (17-20 Jul) had 1,100+ exhibitors and 3,000+ products, with humanoid robots and VLA/world models as a central theme.
organizations._relationship_reason: Watch for model and robot launches; attendance unrealistic.

organizations.What they build: Top Chinese university for robotics/embodied AI; source of spinouts such as RobotEra; its Youth2Real team won two tracks at ICRA 2026 manipulation competitions.
organizations._relationship_reason: Student competition teams are peers; meeting them at ICRA/competitions is the realistic path.

summary:
China leads humanoid volume: Chinese vendors took >97% of H1-2026 humanoid shipments; AgiBot, Unitree, UBTech lead, with Galbot/Galaxea/Fourier as the best-funded challengers.
Money: record embodied-AI funding and an IPO wave in 2026 (Unitree listed at ~$9bn; AgiBot, DEEP Robotics, Leju filing), backed by state funds and carmakers (XPeng).
Demand: factories (UBTech Walker S2, Dobot ATOM), logistics (Geek+) and research/education platforms; state labs (BAAI, Shanghai AI Lab, X-Humanoid) open-source models and datasets.
Relevance to our wedge: cheapest hardware comes from here (Go2 $1.6k, R1 $4.9k, PiPER ~$2.5k, LEMO $3k) and open VLAs/datasets (GO-1, G0, InternVLA-M1, RoboBrain, AgiBot World, RoboMIND) are free to use.
Best entry point: not sponsorship but open-source engagement + hardware purchase: port/benchmark GO-1 or G0 and PiPER/LEMO arms in LeRobot, then approach AgileX/Galaxea/Dobot for edu discounts.
